parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, no documented state violence, detention, or imprisonment of trans visitors, and no sourced entry restriction beyond one documented May 2025 border incident of mockery and questioning by immigration officials. Against that, the combined regime offers no protective machinery (no equality law, hate-crime cover, or registered advocacy), operates an active national censorship baseline treating LGBT expression as 'abnormal' and reaching platforms and foreign performers, and routes transition-related matters through hostile or family-gated institutions. Courts showed narrow capacity (2024 conversion-therapy payout; guards dismissed after 2018 attack), and polls show majority-leaning acceptance. Exposures are humiliation, expression constraint and service friction — not custody — placing this above the 0.45 anchors but below the 0.65 protection-working tier.

entry_documents.exposure: May 2025: immigration officials laughed at, mocked and questioned a visibly trans traveller during a family trip. No document-marker rule, screening regime, or entry refusal is sourced; exposure is discretionary official derision with no stated remedy.
entry_documents.protection: No entry-specific protection documented. The only concession is dependent residency for same-sex partners of legal residents, not a trans-visitor safeguard.
entry_documents.interaction: Border encounter is the first contact; humiliation could escalate into wider scrutiny, but no documented escalation pathway to detention or charge exists.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, detention, custody placement, verification exam, or prosecution of a trans visitor appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Absence of custody records is weakly reassuring in an otherwise richly documented dossier, but no trans-specific detention policy or safeguard is sourced either way.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National censorship baseline (2016 guidelines, extended to platforms) bans 'abnormal sexual behaviour'; rainbow flags barred even inside venues; a foreign drag artist's tour and a trans dancer's shows were curtailed in 2025-26. Resident facilities (dorms, bathrooms, uniforms) discriminate by legal marker.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented for visitors; no public-accommodation protection exists.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Venue and platform rules reach a visibly trans visitor's public presence; resident facility discrimination mainly affects long stays.

care_services.exposure: Adults need parental consent (with proof of parental death) for gender-affirming surgery and legal gender change; online sale of estradiol and blockers banned since Dec 2022 (in-person only); conversion practices remain in routine psychiatric use per Dec 2024 investigation.
care_services.protection: 2024 record damages award against electroshock conversion treatment shows courts can grant relief; seven centres treat trans youth; 2022 consensus recommends puberty blockers.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or continuity care enters a system where disclosure can trigger family-gated or conversion-oriented handling; no visitor-specific care rule is sourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State framing is hostile: 'abnormal sexual behaviour' censorship, 'foreign ideologies' crackdown making activism 'all but extinct', LGBTI organisations barred from registration, 2025 vote against a UN SOGI mandate, textbooks upheld calling homosexuality a disorder.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None institutionalised; a single court payout is the only counter-signal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: This climate sets the tone for how officials treat an outed visitor at border, platform, and venue level, without creating a trans-specific offence.

minors_guardians.exposure: One province alone lets minors apply for gender-marker change; foreign same-sex couples barred from adoption; parental-consent regime pushes disputes inside families. Travelling-minor exposure thin.
minors_guardians.protection: Guardianship-by-agreement (2017) exists unevenly, but notaries impose extra conditions and discipline staff who apply it to same-sex couples.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans parent or travelling minor encounters family-framed gatekeeping rather than a stated entry or custody rule; subnational variation is explicitly unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single 2018 incident: two women in rainbow badges beaten by security guards in the capital. Not a patterned rate; dossier states no trans-specific killing figures exist, so magnitude is unknown rather than low.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Positive state response: the three guards were dismissed shortly after. One 2024 conversion-therapy claim succeeded in court.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Response shows public anti-LGBT violence is treated as sanctionable, but one case cannot establish a reliable protection rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection, no hate-crime coverage, no registered LGBTI organisations, no legal gender recognition; border mockery had no stated recourse. Document rules and screening practice explicitly unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts are narrowly open: record 2024 payout; 2021 notary discipline shows enforcement against facilitation, but litigation route survived.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin formal recourse plus censorship means an outed visitor's realistic remedy is consular or public attention, not domestic equality machinery.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia features a routine police pattern of stops, passport and phone confiscation, hours-long interviews, fines and unofficial files. This dossier documents no analogous recurring police pattern, no confiscation, no fines, and no detention — only a single border-mocking incident. Censorship is expressive rather than custodial, so this rates clearly above 0.35-B.

Kestrel Isles has an actual border regime routing trans travellers to secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow, rarely revised appeals, plus humiliation and cost. Here the border harm is documented but narrower (mockery/questioning, no refusal or screening regime sourced), while an additional national expression-censorship layer exists. Overall exposure and severity are comparable, netting roughly this level.

Meridia has trained respectful border officials, a tribunal hearing detention appeals, written reasons, counsel access and compensation. This dossier shows the opposite institutional posture: derisive officials, no equality law, no hate-crime cover, no registered advocacy, and censorship of LGBT expression. Lacking those protections and facing an active hostile climate, it sits materially below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of absence plus expressive hostility rather than custody. Nothing criminalises trans identity, no trans visitor detention or violence is documented, and courts delivered one landmark payout while guards were dismissed after the only recorded assault — real, if thin, positive signals. Offsetting these: the state offers no equality, hate-crime, or advocacy machinery; an active censorship baseline bars LGBT expression at platform, venue and performance level, reaching a visibly trans visitor's public presence; border officials mocked a trans traveller with no recourse; and transition-related matters are family-gated with conversion practices still routine. Severity therefore sits at humiliation, expression constraint and service friction — not arrest. A traveller who avoids conspicuous expression faces lower exposure, but that is a traveller property, not a jurisdictional protection. Net: Elevated-to-Reduced Risk boundary, 0.57.
